attacks.claim: The limiter uses Date.now with no clamp on elapsed time. A backward clock step makes elapsed negative and tokens go below zero, so a tenant is throttled for a time proportional to the step. This is rare, and the lockout is bounded by the step size.
attacks.evidence: constructor(private now: () => number = Date.now) {} ... b.tokens = Math.min(limits.burst, b.tokens + elapsedSec * limits.ratePerSec);

attacks.claim: The single upstream-429 retry is not charged to the tenant bucket. The sleep ignores client disconnect, and the first response is abandoned without cleanup. When the upstream Retry-After exceeds 5s, the retry fires early and may fail again.
attacks.evidence: await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delay)); res = await upstream.chat(req.body, { signal: req.signal });

attacks.claim: The new route behavior has no tests: the 429 response shape, the upstream retry, the Retry-After cap, and the LRU bound. Only the bucket arithmetic is covered.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: tests for completions.ts, retryAfterMs, or LRU eviction; bucket.test.ts covers only TenantLimiter.

attacks.claim: The default of 20 rps / burst 40 takes effect on deploy for tenants without explicit config. There is no dry-run mode or traffic data showing that no tenant is currently above the default.
attacks.evidence: limits from tenant config, default 20 rps / burst 40

attacks.claim: The log line writes a truncated unsalted SHA-256 of the API key. It is not the key, and the tenant id is already logged next to it. It adds a derivative of the secret to the logs for little benefit.
Config values are not validated. A ratePerSec of 0 gives an infinite wait and an invalid Retry-After header. LRU eviction also resets a tenant to a full burst.
Every rejected request logs at info level with no sampling, so log volume grows with the offending traffic.
attacks.evidence: req.log.info({ tenant: tenant.id, key: keyFingerprint(tenant.apiKey), waitMs }, "tenant rate limited");
